newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thousands of German public workers protest at cuts.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of German public workers protest at cuts.

text.p: Nearly 17,000 German public sector workers marched through central Berlin on Thursday to protest against a law before parliament which they say will cut thousands of jobs in the Berlin area.

The OeTV public sector and DAG white-collar workers' unions held the demonstration one day before the lower house of parliament considers a bill which would decentralise the federal pension authority (BfA).
"We are protesting against the loss of up to 13,000 jobs," said DAG state director Hartmut Friedrich said during a rally beside the war-damaged Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church.
"These jobs were safe for decades and now they are being called into question."
The BfA is Berlin's largest service-sector employer with over 23,000 employees and the unions said the city had been unfairly targeted for cutbacks since German unification in 1990.
"Berlin cannot continue to be abused to ensure jobs in other states and regions," the unions said in a statement.
